# RustyNES v2.6.10 "Inference"

The cartridge meets the synthesiser, and simulation could not have asked the question.

v2.6.9 landed five cartridge boards — UxROM, CNROM, AxROM, MMC1, MMC3 — verified across 141 co-simulation gates, every one matching the oracle on every compared cycle. **Not one of them had ever been through Quartus.** Building that release's bitstream is what asked, and Analysis & Synthesis refused the design outright.

## What was wrong

```text
Error (276003): Cannot convert all sets of registers into RAM megafunctions
```

`chr` was written from **two separate `always_ff` blocks** — the ROM load port and the CHR-RAM write path. An array with two writers in two different always blocks cannot infer as a single M10K, so Quartus kept 128 KB of CHR in flip-flops: **1,048,576 registers against roughly 166,000** on a 5CSEBA6U23I7.

Folding both writers into one port through an `always_comb` mux fixes it. The loader takes priority, which is safe because the CPU is held during ROM load, so `chr_wr` cannot be asserted at the same time.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Analysis & Synthesis | **unsuccessful**, 1 error | successful, **0 errors** |
| `prg` / `chr` / `prg_ram` | not inferred | all three `altsyncram` |
| total block memory bits | — | **666,054** |

## Why it survived 141 green gates

**Simulation cannot ask this question.** Verilator accepts both forms without complaint — two writers or one, the behaviour is identical, and every one of those 141 gates compares *behaviour*. Only a synthesiser distinguishes them, and until a bitstream was demanded, nothing ran one over the cartridge.

This is v2.6.6's finding one layer out. That release established that an M10K read is *registered*, and rewrote 40 KiB of asynchronously-read cartridge that would have cost 393,216 registers. This one establishes the sequel: a correctly registered memory still will not infer if it has **two writers**. The rule that came out of v2.6.6 — "synchronous read with a registered address" — was necessary and not sufficient.

## The bitstream v2.6.9 could not produce

`releases/RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.6.10.rbf`, built from this RTL, verified against the Quartus **reports** rather than the exit code (Quartus has been observed here to exit 0 after aborting), and attached to the GitHub release on both repositories.

v2.6.9 shipped **without** a bitstream and said so in its body, because a published version is immutable in this project and the fix was not yet verified against the suite. That disclosure stands; this release is where the artifact arrives.

## Verification

- **Co-simulation suite re-run in full** against the new write port — muxing it changes when a CHR-RAM write lands relative to a load, and only the suite can say whether that is observable.
- **The emulation core is unchanged**: no chip crate changed, so AccuracyCoin 141/141 (RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction.
- Timing figures are reported at the **binding corners**, discovered from the report by pattern rather than from a fixed list — the v2.6.7 lesson that a gate reading one corner reports the margin of the corner it reads.

## Timing closed, and the fitter was throttling itself

The first v2.6.10 compile **failed timing** at −0.265 ns on the framework's HDMI PLL path, and the Fitter log said why in its own words:

```text
Info (171003): Fitter is performing an Auto Fit compilation,
which may decrease Fitter effort to reduce compilation time
```

Quartus was deliberately spending *less* effort because it judged the design easy. The `.qsf` carried **no optimisation assignments at all**, so it was running defaults. Two documented settings fix it — `FITTER_EFFORT "STANDARD FIT"` (the documented setting for speed-optimised designs, against the Auto Fit default) and `OPTIMIZATION_MODE "Aggressive Performance"` (whose caveat is that it backfires at very high utilisation; this design sits at **53% ALMs, 12% block memory**). `PLACEMENT_EFFORT_MULTIPLIER` is deliberately **not** set: it cannot be raised above 1.0 directly, and the documented route to more placement effort is the optimisation mode.

**The seed sweep then found the shape, which is the real result:**

| | seed 4 | seed 2 | seed 5 | seed 1 | seed 6 | seed 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto Fit | **−0.265** | — | **−0.059** | — | — | — |
| full effort | +0.027 | +0.229 | +0.282 | +0.406 | +0.464 | **+0.531** |

Under Auto Fit the two seeds tried both **failed**. Under full effort **all six close**, spanning +0.027 to +0.531 — the effort settings move the entire distribution across zero, and the seed only picks where in it you land. This project had been pinned to seed 4, **the worst of the six**.

**Pinned at seed 3: worst setup +0.531 ns, worst hold +0.099 ns**, both at the binding corners (Slow −40C and Fast −40C), discovered from the report by pattern rather than assumed — the v2.6.7 lesson that a gate reading one corner reports that corner's margin. Slow 100C reads +0.173 and would have looked fine throughout the failure.

**Stated honestly: +0.531 ns is "the best of six placements", not headroom the design earned.** A seed samples placements rather than improving the design, and the next RTL edit re-rolls it. The durable part is the effort settings, which are reproducible for a reason. The build is byte-identical across two independent compiles at this seed (md5 `94b7d855…`).

## What this release does NOT claim

**No hardware has run this bitstream.** Timing closure and a produced `.rbf` are claimed; a booting core is not. The palette, the video timing constants, the audio absolute level and its band-limiting remain unverified *by construction* — every gate in the ladder compares something upstream of all four.

**Rung 6 does not close.** No DE10-Nano and no SuperStation One are attached to this machine, confirmed by checking rather than assumed.
